label: first copied token (d/b/j/f) fed back in short sequences where j comes next
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.005% of steps). 85% of activation mass is at step L+1, where the first copied token is fed back in (prev_tok = <DEL>, recall_idx 1). It fires almost only for short sequences (L=3 or 4; L=3 is 28x enriched) and mostly when the fed-back first token is d, b, j or f. It is strongest when the token being output (orig(1)) or the one after it (orig(2)) is j: the top examples are d j j, j j j, b j j, d j t. A weak secondary activation sometimes shows up one step later (recall_idx 2). It does not fire during the original phase (about 5% of mass), on the delimiter, or in long sequences. The conjunction leaves many false positives (precision about 0.24), so the exact token conditions are only partly captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=d (+3.85), phase=2 & out_tok=f (+3.38), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=j (+3.14), phase=2 & out_tok=j (+3.06), orig0=f (+2.68), phase=2 & in_tok=b (+2.59).
